summary: The deliberately injected fault CHG-9a260cd9 (20:56:38Z) caused a full-stack processing freeze - every component, including Kafka's internal scheduler and Prometheus's own self-scrape, stopped executing for roughly one hour (~21:52-22:55 UTC, corroborated independently at 21:48:38-22:56:29 by Kafka's own logs) - collapsing transaction throughput by over 95% before the pipeline resumed on its own with no lasting damage.
reasoning: Anchored to the 20:56:38Z injection and correctly ruled out an earlier redis2 restart/CLUSTERDOWN episode as a prior, resolved incident (finished 16 minutes before the injection). Found a synchronized 'up' scrape gap across every job (go-server, all 3 enrichers, kafka, redis, Prometheus's own self-scrape) and an independent Kafka-internal task-scheduler gap, concluding this represented a stack-wide freeze. Explicitly investigated redis1's 5MB maxmemory/allkeys-lru cap (vs redis2/redis3's unlimited/noeviction) and found real evictions climbing, but concluded via a 9-hour get_metrics query that the value had been constant since approximately 16:30 - over 4 hours before the injection - and set it aside as a long-standing baseline condition rather than the injected fault, alongside a separately-flagged pre-existing Go format-string logging bug.
